inputs.evidence: All proposition documents, bundle and pricing sheets, channel plans, product-team decks and message exports must be read, and the same claim about components, prices, timing or channels can differ between documents.

workflow.evidence: Many dependent stages: list every claim, classify it as consistent, conflicting or missing, compare document dates, build the dependency view and revise earlier outputs when a later one shows a gap. The reconciliation is shown for approval before the deck and register are built.

deliverables.evidence: Three interdependent deliverables, a workbook, a deck and a dependency register, plus draft messages to each conflict owner; a change in one forces a revision in the others.

situation: A proposition such as Household 3.0 combines components, prices, timing and channels, and many teams describe it in their own documents. When the documents disagree, nobody knows which statement is current, what is still missing and which team has to resolve what before launch.

prompt.outcome: Create three review-ready outputs for [proposition scope]: a reconciliation workbook with a claim-by-claim comparison and a conflict log, a deck of no more than [slide limit] slides with the reconciled proposition, the open decisions and what each team must resolve, and a dependency register with item, depends on, owner and needed-by date.
prompt.inputs: All proposition documents, bundle and pricing sheets, channel plans and product-team decks in [the input folder], plus the approved Teams exports in [the approved messages]. List every claim about components, prices, timing and channels, mark each as consistent, conflicting or missing, and note which document is the most recent. Show both sides of every conflict with their sources.
prompt.doneWhen: The workbook, the deck and the register are saved in [the output folder]; every claim has a status and a source; every conflict lists both sides and is marked as an open decision; the register leaves an owner or date blank when no document names one; and draft messages to [the conflict owners] are ready but not sent.
prompt.constraints: Never choose a winner between conflicting claims: do not prefer the most recent document and do not fill a missing date or price from another document. Do not invent owners, dates, prices or approvals. Mark gaps and assumptions, do not use sources I have not named, and do not contact customers or colleagues.
prompt.approval: Show me the reconciliation and the conflict log first. Build the deck and the dependency register and save anything only after my OK, and send nothing.
